task: Bangkok editorial research batch 2 (research only; no live app data changed)
popularity_method: No citywide popularity measure has been collected. Coverage breadth is measured for batch selection only (windowed, publisher-family-deduped scan); it is a research-selection signal, never a popularity score.
researcher: zcode-main (ZCode orchestrator + coverage-scan and 6 research subagents), 2026-11-07

entities.scope_notes: Administrative khet (~9.59 km², pop ~67,388 in 2020) along the Phahonyothin corridor with sharply different subareas (Ari, Saphan Khwai, Sanam Pao, Pradiphat, Samsen Nai). Research-verified: the khet's namesake BTS Phaya Thai + ARL terminus sit in Ratchathewi, just outside the khet (app-polygon check confirms); inside stations are Ari, Sanam Pao, Saphan Khwai + SRT Sam Sen. Green 9's likely basis is the Royal Thai Army compound and other state land (controlled access, not public parkland — inference; 14.8 ha unmapped). Victory Monument's attribution is conflicting (app polygon includes the roundabout; sources place it in Ratchathewi).
entities.selection_rationale: District #4 with broad coverage; district-level counterpart to the pilot's st.ari findings; where the 14.8 ha of mapped parkland actually sit.

entities.name_th: ป้อมปราบศัตรูพ่าย
entities.scope_notes: Administrative khet (~1.93 km², pop ~41,524 in 2020, density ~21,504/km² — among Bangkok's densest) between the Golden Mount and Chinatown. Research-verified: the Chinatown Soi Nana bar strip and Bangkok Kunsthalle are in khwaeng Pom Prap; Woeng Nakhon Kasem is in Samphanthawong (the app alias list includes it — a data-level correction for reviewers); Rommaninat Park is in Phra Nakhon; Wat Ratchanatdaram's attribution is conflicting. Green 9 rests on the free Golden Mount compound and the Khlong Ong Ang promenade (researcher inference; only 0.7 ha mapped parks).
entities.selection_rationale: District #3 with broad independent coverage; owns the Chinatown Soi Nana bars and Khlong Thom the pilot placed outside Samphanthawong; green 9 vs 0.7 ha park test.

entities.scope_notes: 800 m nearest-stop catchment around BTS Charoen Nakhon (Gold Line G2) on the Charoen Nakhon Road corridor. District split (app data): Khlong San 75%, Bang Rak 25% — the 25% being the east-bank pier strip the circle sweeps across the river bend. Research-verified: ICONSIAM is inside and adjacent (OSM mall polygon ~0.14 km from the station; exits 1–3 bridge directly in; River Park end ~0.47 km). The Gold Line has three stations and never crosses the river (1.74–1.8 km total); the transport 10 plausibly reflects the pier cluster plus buses rather than rail service alone (researcher inference; score untouched).
entities.selection_rationale: Rank #2/133 with thin independent coverage — the high-score/low-coverage pattern; transport 10 for a Gold Line feeder needed a mechanism check.

entities.scope_notes: 800 m nearest-stop catchment around BTS Nana. District split (app data): Watthana 48%, Khlong Toei 44%, Pathum Wan 8%. NOT the Chinatown Soi Nana — that cocktail-bar strip sits in Pom Prap Sattru Phai inside st.wat-mangkon's catchment (batch-2 verified). Research-verified: Nana Plaza ~255–300 m inside; Bumrungrad campus straddles the NW boundary (frontage ~415–450 m inside, geotagged center ~710 m outside the polygon); Benchasiri ~1.7 km east and Lumphini ~1.6–1.7 km south both outside — green 10 is not reproducible from in-unit geometry (1.4 ha mapped, identity unresolved).
entities.selection_rationale: Popular-but-contested nightlife identity; the Soi Nana name confusion is a Q01 test; green 10 with 1.4 ha park is a green-geometry outlier.

entities.scope_notes: 800 m nearest-stop catchment around BTS Ratchathewi, entirely within Ratchathewi khet but not the whole khet (which extends far north on Phahonyothin). Research-verified outside: Baiyoke Tower II (~1.28 km ENE), Santiphap Park (~1.65 km NNE, Ratchathewi khet's north), Suan Pakkad Palace Museum (~0.81 m NNE, nearer BTS Phaya Thai). No named public park verified inside (app 1.0 ha unmatched; OSM shows none). The Ratchathewi flyover closed 15–16 Jan 2025 with reconstruction due by Apr 2028.
entities.selection_rationale: Rank #3/133 and the only station area with 'some' measured coverage; safety 5 (lowest in the research set) vs vibe 10 needed testing.

entities.scope_notes: 800 m nearest-stop catchment around MRT Wat Mangkon (Blue Line, opened 2019), straddling Pom Prap Sattru Phai 51.4% / Samphanthawong 48.6%. Note for reviewers: Wikipedia attributes the station itself to Samphanthawong while the app's district split gives Pom Prap the majority. Research-verified inside: Wat Mangkon Kamalawat temple (~54 m to geotag, Pom Prap side — refuting a pilot note that placed it 'just outside the khet') and the northwestern end of the Chinatown Soi Nana bar strip (~414–447 m; the lane straddles the boundary). Research-verified outside: Wat Traimit and Odean Circle (st.hua-lamphong side), Khlong Ong Ang and Rommaninat Park (st.sam-yot side), Golden Mount (~0.91 km).
entities.selection_rationale: Boundary control: catchment split Pom Prap 51.4% / Samphanthawong 48.6%, straddling the pilot's Samphanthawong findings on both sides.
